about: The orlop and the hold of the frigate Commonwealth as built, 1797 (docs/shipkit-14): the berth deck's beams overhead, the orlop's after and fore platforms with their rooms, the cable tiers amidships between them, and the hold under them: the ceiling, the keelson and its mast steps, the limbers, the ballast, the pump well, the casks in their tiers, the shot lockers, the magazines with their light rooms and filling room, the spirit room, the bread rooms and the store rooms. Lengths in feet (_ft) and inches (_in) unless a key says metres (_m) or pixels (_px). Each value carries its source; 'estimate' means period practice or proportion, not a drawing. orlop.py reads this file

sources.orlop_1849: NARA 75841362, 'Orlop Decks of the U.S. Frigate Constitution', Navy Yard Boston, May 1849, scale four feet to the inch (public domain; Commons' 3840 px rendering, measured only, never committed): stern on the left, starboard at the bottom. The after platform (light room, filling room, passage, bread rooms, the cockpit, the spirit room and after hatches, state rooms, store rooms, the slop room, the captain's store room, the dispensary), the open middle (the pumps and main mast in a casing, shot and chain lockers on the middle line, the cable tiers either side over the water in the hold, its beams drawn across) and the fore platform (coal and sand, the sail rooms, the general store room and its counter, the racks for stores, the fore mast, the scuttles to the light room, the magazine and the block room, the master's store room, marine clothing, the paint room)
sources.hold_1849: NARA 75841358, 'Magazines and Hold of the U.S. Frigate Constitution', the same set and scale: the bread room, light room, passage and after magazine aft, the shell rooms and the spirit room, the main hold's water (numbered iron tanks by then) round the pump well, the main mast, the shot lockers and chain lockers, the forward magazine with its light room and passage, the fore peak and block room
sources.period: estimate: the period's practice for an American frigate of the 1790s where neither drawing shows a part, and where 1849 differs from 1797: water in casks (the iron tanks came in the 1810s), the anchor cables hemp (chain came in the 1820s and 30s, so the 1849 chain lockers are a spare cable's and the hawsers' tiers), no shell rooms (no shells in 1797: they are store rooms), no coal (the coal and sand room keeps sand for the decks), and the shingle ballast over iron pigs

registration.note: each plan's 3840 px rendering, stern on the left, starboard at the bottom, carried to the ship by the masts as the gun deck's plan is (gundeck_1797.json): between the main and fore masts an item keeps its share of the way from one to the other, aft of the main mast and forward of the fore mast its distance from the mast at the plan's scale. The masts are where each one's axis passes the orlop's top (orlop) or the ceiling's top at the keelson (hold). The scales are the written sizes' (orlop: the bread room's 16 ft 3 in, the light room's 10 ft 0 in and the bread room's 12 ft 3 in across, 19.6 to 19.7 px a foot; hold: the forward light room's 17 ft 2 in and the magazine's 23 ft 4 in): the renderings differ, the sheets being scanned at different widths

heights.note: the decks' heights at midships, all estimate until the midship section (NARA 75841385) is read: the berth deck's top from the berth deck slice (13) when it lands, until then the gun deck's well floor (gundeck_1797.json wells: 6 ft 10 in under the gun deck's top); the orlop's top under it by orlop_below_berth_ft, following the berth deck's sheer (each deck parallel to the one above it); the keelson's top 3 ft over the rabbet (spars_1795.json step: the masts step on it); the ceiling's inside face 16 in in from the moulded surface (the gun deck's wall: frames and ceiling, specs_1795.json inside), never lower than the floor heads' flat, floor_over_rabbet_in over the rabbet, beside the keelson
heights.depth_of_hold_note: Humphreys' 1794 proportions give the 44s a depth of hold of 13 ft 6 in (the ceiling at midships to the top of the lower deck's beams): build.json orlop.depth_of_hold_ft reports ours against it

ceiling.note: the hold's ceiling: the inside planking from the limber strake beside the keelson up to the orlop's clamp (the berth deck's own spirketting and clamp above it are slice 13's): oak 4 in thick, in strakes of 12 in with a seam between each (estimate), running from the after bread room's bulkhead to the fore peak's. Aft and forward of those the run and the bow close in to the deadwood: the after bread room and the fore peak are floored at the floor heads' flat
ceiling.limber_note: the limber passage either side of the keelson (water runs to the pump well along it), covered by the limber boards: 1.5 in, loose, laid from the keelson's side to the limber strake

keelson.note: oak, 15 in sided and 15 in moulded on the floors (estimate: the period's proportion, a little over the keel's 14 in), scarphed, with a step for each mast: a chock on it with a mortise for the heel's tenon (spars.py: the tenon square, 0.3 of the mast's diameter, 0.25 of it long). Its top 3 ft over the rabbet (spars_1795.json step)

orlop.note: the orlop's after and fore platforms, planked flat across (pine, 3 in, on beams 10 in sided, 9 in moulded, 4 ft apart: estimate), each from its end bulkhead to the side; amidships between them the cable tiers: beams only (the plan's four across the middle), each tier floored with battens on them where the cables lie (2 by 4 in, 2 in apart: estimate), and the shot and cable lockers on the middle line
orlop.tier_beams_note: the plan draws four beams across the middle (an inch, 20 px wide each): those in the open between the pumps' casing and the shot lockers. The rest of the middle's beams follow at the platforms' pitch

rooms.note: the platforms' rooms, from the plan: each [x0, x1] px along, [y0, y1] px across (from the top of the sheet; the centreline is 509), mirrored where the plan draws a pair. Partitions 1.5 in deal on 3 in posts (estimate), doors as the gun deck's cabin doors' openings (2 ft 3 in by 5 ft, or the headroom less 3 in). The bread rooms and the magazine's filling room lined with tin (the period's practice against rats and sparks)

after.name: LightRoomAft
after.note: the light room: a lantern behind glass lights the magazine below (the hold's after magazine) through the filling room's floor

after.name: FillingRoom
after.note: the filling room over the after magazine: cartridges filled here, lined with tin, the scuttle down to the magazine

after.name: BreadRoomMid
after.note: 16 ft 3 in by 12 ft 3 in, tin-lined

after.name: BreadRoomSide
after.note: each side outboard of the middle bread room, from the after bulkhead to the cabins

after.name: Dispensary
after.note: the surgeon's dispensary next to the cockpit

fore.name: SailRoom
fore.note: 10 ft 1 in long, the sails stowed rolled on shelves

fore.name: SandRoom
fore.note: the plan's coal and sand room: sand only in 1797 (holystoning, the galley's hearth)

fore.name: GeneralStoreRoom
fore.note: the boatswain's general store room: a counter on the middle line, racks for stores curving along each side

hatches.note: the orlop's hatches, inside sizes as written on the plan: the spirit room hatch (5 ft 6 in by 5 ft 1 in) and the after hatch (5 ft 4 in by 5 ft 1 in) in the cockpit, the scuttles down to the hold's store rooms (written 1 ft 9 in square), the scuttles forward to the light room (1 ft 10 in by 1 ft 10 in), the magazine (2 ft 4 in square) and the block room (2 ft 8 in square). Coamings 6 in high, 3 in thick (estimate); ladders down where a hatch leads to a room people work in

middle.note: the middle line between the platforms (plan): a casing round the pumps and the main mast down to the well (6 ft 8 in across), then the shot lockers (4 ft 6 in and 5 ft 4 in long) and the cable lockers (5 ft 3 in and 6 ft 0 in; the 1849 chain lockers), each a box of 2 in deal on posts from the hold's ceiling up to the berth deck's beams, open over the orlop's beams where the shot is passed up. Each [x0, x1] px, the half width 3 ft 4 in

hold.note: the hold's rooms (hold plan, x px along it): aft the bread room in the run, the light room, the passage and the after magazine; then the store rooms (the 1849 shell rooms) either side and the spirit room between them; the main hold from its after bulkhead to the forward magazine's, with the pump well round the main mast and the pumps; then the forward magazine with its light room over its after part on the starboard side... and its passage, the fore peak and the block room under the fore mast

casks.note: the water in casks, two tiers on the ballast in the main hold either side of the pump well and forward of it (the 1849 tanks' room): leaguers (150 gal) in the ground tier, butts (108 gal) over them in the cantlines, bung up, lying fore and aft, each bedded on the shingle (the period's stowage). Sizes [length, bilge, head] m are the stores kit's Cask_Leaguer, Cask_Butt and PowderBarrel (stores.json, Nov 17), whose meshes take their places when they land

ballast.note: iron pigs (3 ft by 6 in by 6 in, about 300 lb) laid fore and aft on the ceiling either side of the keelson, then shingle over them to the ground tier's bilge, levelled (estimate: the period's stowage)

hold.bulkheads_note: hold plan x px: the after light room's fore side and the passage (4 ft) aft of the after magazine, which the mizzen passes through to its step on the keelson; the magazine's fore bulkhead (23 ft 4 in on); the spirit room; the main hold's after bulkhead; the fore magazine and its passage. The spirit room's fore bulkhead stands at 1203, not the plan's 1154.5: registered by the masts, the orlop plan's spirit room hatch reaches 2 ft past the hold plan's bulkhead, and the hatch and its ladder lead into the spirit room

budget_note: the plan's figure for slice 14 (the orlop and hold, loaded only when below: build.json orlop.triangles): a starting point, not a ceiling (Bean, Nov 12: frame rate is the only hard limit), so the build reports the count against it and never fails on it

meets.note: the orlop's and hold's parts that meet another part of the ship (or each other) by design, each pair with why and how far (in) either may go into the other; every other meeting fails the build (build_frigate's orlop_room, deck.room), as gundeck_1797.json's meets

cables.note: the hemp cables (22 in: the 44-gun frigate's bower, period tables) flaked down in the tiers: two coils each side of the middle line, 120 fathoms each about 3.2 m across and four layers deep, each layer a flat spiral (estimate). The cables come down the berth deck's cable scuttles from the manger (slice 13 hands over where)
